title: Ramadan: the early meal
hookLine: eat before dawn, for there is blessing in it (Bukhari)

lines: A DRUM IN THE DARK STREETS.
cards: Three forty-five in the morning. In old neighborhoods of Cairo or Istanbul, during Ramadan, a man may still walk the dark streets beating a small drum and calling out names, waking people up.
In a suburban kitchen, a phone alarm goes off, and someone stumbles in, eyes half shut, and starts the kettle. Oats. Dates.
Eggs. A lot of water. Nobody's hungry at this hour.
Everyone's eating anyway. The Prophet ﷺ gave the reason in one line.

teach.b: The meal is called suhur, from sahar, the last part of the night, just before dawn.
The line is in Bukhari: take the suhur meal, for in suhur there is blessing. Barakah. More than a benefit: a quiet abundance, when a little turns out to be enough.
The practical side is obvious, too: a long day without food or water goes better if you start it fed. But when do you stop?

teach.h: A WHITE THREAD AND A BLACK THREAD.
teach.b: The Qur'an, in Surah al-Baqarah, says eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. And there's a lovely story about that verse, also in Bukhari.
A companion named Adi ibn Hatim took it literally. He put a white thread and a black thread under his pillow and kept looking at them all night, waiting to tell them apart. He couldn't.
In the morning he told the Prophet, who, in one telling, teased him that his pillow must be very wide, and explained: it means the darkness of the night and the whiteness of the day.
The white thread is the first line of light along the horizon.

teach.h: ABOUT FIFTY VERSES BEFORE THE PRAYER.
teach.b: Another companion, Zayd ibn Thabit, said they ate suhur with the Prophet and then stood for the prayer; asked how long between them, he said: about as long as reciting fifty verses. So the meal was late, close to dawn.

teach.h: A SMALL MEAL, IN THE DARK, ON PURPOSE.
teach.b: A small, deliberate meal in the dark, the last thing before the day's long quiet.

how: During Ramadan, Muslims who fast wake before dawn to eat suhur, often dates, water and simple food, and stop eating and drinking at the start of dawn, when the time of fajr begins.

games.q: you're Adi ibn Hatim. the verse says eat until the white thread is distinct from the black. what do you do?
o: put a white and a black thread under your pillow and watch them
stop eating at midnight to be safe
games.why: he watched the threads all night and couldn't tell them apart. the Prophet explained: it's the darkness of night and the whiteness of day (Bukhari).

practice: Picture tomorrow morning, a little earlier than you usually wake: where the glass is, where you'll sit, drinking slowly in the dark before the day starts asking things of you.
If you fast, plan your suhur the same way, simple, late, on purpose; if you don't, settle on one glass of water before anything else, and say to yourself: blessing before dawn.

wordCard.voice: Suhur. The meal before dawn in Ramadan, eaten late, for in it there is blessing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the pre-dawn meal, from sahar, the last part of the night.

carryVoice: Your line: blessing before dawn. The first thread of light tells you when to stop. Day one hundred twenty-one.
